title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: Follow the Cash — Ten Years of P&L, Balance Sheet & Cash Conversion Forensics

epigraph.quote: Accounting profit is an opinion shaped by depreciation schedules and accruals; cash flow from operations is a fact.
epigraph.author: Forensic accounting principle

web_blocks.html: A ten-year forensic review from FY15 through H1 FY27 reveals steady long-term compounding. Zydus tripled revenue from ₹8,651 crore to ₹27,148 crore in FY26, reaching ₹30,378 crore TTM [1]. Over the same span, operating profit grew nearly fivefold from ₹1,756 crore to ₹8,475 crore [1]. Three forensic inflections must be unpacked separately: the FY22 divestment gain, the FY26 cash-conversion dip, and the FY25–H1 FY27 M&A debt expansion.

web_blocks.html:
Four Forensic Takeaways from the 10-Year Numbers & Footnotes:
1. Cash Conversion Anomaly in FY26: Over FY20–FY25, Zydus converted operating profit into cash reliably. CFO peaked at ₹6,781 crore (122% CFO/EBITDA) with ₹5,139 crore FCF in FY25 [1]. In FY26, CFO fell to ₹2,117 crore (44% CFO/EBITDA) and FCF turned -₹530 crore [1]. Inventory Days spiked from 227 to 282 to build launch and acquired European/UK stock [1]. The $120 million Mirabegron settlement and higher tax outflows also weighed on cash. Yet the board approved a ₹1,100 crore buyback while cutting dividend payout from 24% to 2% [1][7].
2. Balance Sheet, Goodwill KAM & Unrecognized Tax Losses: Between Mar 2024 and Sep 2026, Borrowings rose ₹13,162 crore to ₹13,966 crore. Fixed Assets plus CWIP rose ₹14,543 crore to ₹29,334 crore, while Investments reached ₹8,348 crore [1]. Consolidated goodwill climbed to ~₹7,543 crore, including ₹4,032.2 crore at 69.85%-owned Zydus Wellness Products. Auditors flag this goodwill as a recurring Key Audit Matter after ₹219.6 crore of FY25 impairments. Unrecognized deferred tax assets on subsidiary losses doubled from ₹613 crore (Mar 2022) to ₹1,229.1 crore by March 31, 2026. D&A also surged from ₹764 crore (FY24) to ₹2,002 crore TTM [1].
3. Ongoing US Antitrust Litigation Tail: Zydus Pharmaceuticals (USA) remains a defendant in multi-state US generic drug price-fixing suits dating to 2019. In September 2026, Zydus USA agreed to pay $5.9 million to settle indirect-reseller claims without admitting wrongdoing. Broader state AG and bellwether trials still run through 2028 with no expected reimbursements. CRISIL (Sep 2026) explicitly cites this litigation as a credit-rating sensitivity.
4. ROCE vs. WACC Spread & Liquidity Cushion: Consolidated ROCE stood at 22% (FY24), 24% (FY25), and 21% (FY26), clearing ~10–11% INR WACC [1]. CRISIL verifies healthy liquidity: ₹7,465 crore cash/mutual funds as of Mar 2026, 13% bank-line utilization on ₹3,400 crore limits, and 22.5x interest coverage. Sustaining ~18–20%+ ROCE on the enlarged ₹55,607 crore asset base is the central test of FY27–FY29.

H1 FY27 Accounting vs. Operating Reality: Surface-level readers can misread Q2 FY27 bottom-line trends. Reported Q2 FY27 Net Profit fell 25% YoY to ₹928 crore from ₹1,239 crore a year earlier, even though revenue grew 29% [1][3]. Operating profit held firm near ₹1,894 crore at a 24.0% EBITDA margin, matching management's full-year guidance [3][4]. The net-profit squeeze came from two below-the-line items: quarterly depreciation rose to ₹604 crore (from ₹238 crore in Q4 FY25) on acquired intangibles, while quarterly interest climbed to ₹187 crore (from ₹77 crore) on M&A debt [1][3]. Tracking cash flow from operations alongside net profit prevents misreading this acquisition accounting.

book_paragraphs: Now let's put on our forensic accountant's visor and read all ten years of Zydus's numbers side by side, because the balance sheet always tells the story that quarterly press releases gloss over.

First, look at the long-term earnings power. From FY15 to FY26, sales grew from ₹8,651 crore to ₹27,148 crore, and Operating Profit expanded nearly fivefold from ₹1,756 crore to ₹8,475 crore. Along the way, watch out for one optical trap in FY22: reported Net Profit jumped to ₹4,618 crore that year, only to drop to ₹2,092 crore in FY23. Nothing broke in FY23; FY22 was simply inflated by ₹2,581 crore of Other Income from divesting the Animal Health business. Strip that out, and Zydus's core operating profit climbed steadily every single year from ₹3,342 crore in FY22 to ₹8,475 crore in FY26.

Second, examine the sharp cash-flow divergence in FY26. Between FY20 and FY25, Zydus was a cash-printing machine—generating ₹20,996 crore of cumulative operating cash flow and converting 122% of EBITDA into cash in FY25 (₹6,781 crore CFO, ₹5,139 crore Free Cash Flow). Then, in FY26, even as reported Net Profit hit a record ₹5,124 crore, CFO fell by more than two-thirds to ₹2,117 crore (44% of EBITDA) and Free Cash Flow dipped to -₹530 crore. Why? Look at the ratio table: Inventory Days surged from 202 days in FY24 to 227 in FY25 and 282 in FY26, absorbing massive working capital alongside the $120 million Mirabegron litigation settlement—even as the board approved a ₹1,100 crore buyback and cut dividend payout from 24% to 2%.

Third, trace the balance sheet and audit footnotes between March 2024 and September 2026. Total assets nearly doubled from ₹28,834 crore to ₹55,607 crore. Fixed Assets and CWIP jumped from ₹14,791 crore to ₹29,334 crore, while Borrowings climbed from ₹804 crore to ₹13,966 crore. Digging into the audit footnotes reveals three subtler watchpoints: consolidated goodwill has climbed to roughly ₹7,543 crore (including ₹4,032.2 crore at Zydus Wellness Products, a recurring Key Audit Matter after ₹219.6 crore of FY25 impairments); unrecognized deferred tax assets on subsidiary losses doubled to ₹1,229.1 crore by March 2026; and US generic price-fixing antitrust litigation runs through 2028 despite a $5.9 million indirect-reseller class settlement in September 2026. Even so, FY26 ROCE held at 21.1%, Net Debt to EBITDA remains a conservative 0.62x, and CRISIL highlights ₹7,465 crore of cash and mutual funds plus 22.5x interest coverage. The forensic verdict is clear: the balance sheet is still healthy, but the margin for sloppy working capital, goodwill write-downs, or adverse antitrust payouts is now much smaller than it was two years ago.

A ten-year forensic audit of Zydus Lifesciences's financial statements reveals a business with high underlying profitability punctuated by two distinct capital-allocation cycles. From fiscal 2016 through fiscal 2020, debt rose to nearly eight thousand crore rupees to fund Heinz India while US generic margins compressed. From fiscal 2021 through fiscal 2024, disciplined cash harvesting—assisted by the Animal Health divestment and high-margin US launches—slashed debt by ninety percent to just eight hundred four crore rupees while lifting ROCE to twenty-four percent.

Between fiscal 2025 and September 2026, Zydus entered its second major investment cycle. Gross borrowings climbed from three thousand two hundred thirteen crore rupees in March 2025 to twelve thousand four hundred ninety-six crore in March 2026 and thirteen thousand nine hundred sixty-six crore by September 2026, funding Amplitude Surgical, Comfort Click, Naturell, Agenus's California biologics plants, and Assertio Holdings. Fixed assets more than doubled from thirteen thousand one hundred thirty-four crore to twenty-seven thousand six hundred ninety-eight crore over the same eighteen-month window.

Crucially, because Zydus holds eight thousand three hundred forty-eight crore rupees in investments and cash equivalents, net debt remains a manageable zero point six two times EBITDA. The balance sheet is nowhere near distress, but the combination of higher interest expense, elevated depreciation and intangible amortization, recurring goodwill impairment scrutiny, two hundred eighty-two inventory days, and ongoing US antitrust bellwether litigation means free cash flow generation in fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 will be the ultimate litmus test of whether this acquisition spree created enduring economic value.

Reading ten years of audited balance sheets and cash-flow statements strips away storytelling and leaves only capital-allocation truth. Between fiscal 2016 and fiscal 2026, Zydus nearly tripled its revenue from nine thousand four hundred twenty-seven crore rupees to twenty-seven thousand one hundred forty-eight crore rupees, while expanding operating profit from roughly two thousand three hundred crore to eight thousand four hundred seventy-five crore. Over that entire decade, equity dilution was virtually nonexistent, allowing per-share intrinsic value to compound directly for continuing owners.

The single biggest question mark emerging from the fiscal 2026 and September 2026 financial statements is the return on recent M&A capital. With gross borrowings at thirteen thousand nine hundred sixty-six crore rupees, fixed assets at twenty-seven thousand six hundred ninety-eight crore, consolidated goodwill near seven thousand five hundred forty-three crore, and Zydus Wellness absorbing higher Euro-debt interest and intangible amortization, investors must watch fiscal 2027 and 2028 cash conversion closely. If operating cash flow rebounds above sixty-five to seventy-five percent of EBITDA, the acquisition cycle will be vindicated; if it stagnates below fifty percent, debt service will weigh on future compounding.

Ultimately, the ten-year financial record shows a business capable of twenty-one to twenty-four percent returns on capital employed when not weighed down by integration capex. Watching borrowings of thirteen thousand nine hundred sixty-six crore rupees pay down as acquisition cash flows mature will be the defining financial story of fiscal 2028.

book_subsections.title: Reading the Depreciation & Interest Step-Up in H1 FY27
paragraphs: Look at the quarterly progression in the blind data: quarterly Depreciation jumped from ₹238 crore in Q4 FY25 to ₹508 crore in Q4 FY26 and ₹604 crore in Q2 FY27, while quarterly Interest climbed from ₹77 crore to ₹187 crore over the same span. That is the accounting footprint of intangibles amortization and Euro/GBP acquisition debt.

Because Net Profit in Q2 FY27 was ₹928 crore versus ₹1,239 crore a year earlier despite 29% revenue growth, surface-level readers might assume the core business slowed. In reality, operating profit held near ₹1,894 crore; the bottom-line squeeze came from upfront Saroglitazar launch spend plus higher D&A and interest.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When Total Assets double in thirty months through M&A, rising depreciation and interest quietly eat into net profit even when EBITDA looks fine. Watch Return on Capital Employed—and insist on seeing Inventory Days fall back from 282—before declaring the acquisitions a triumph.
